transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because my head just feels foggy lately. I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, dates for exhibits, and even which volunteer I already called. It’s frustrating.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?
I don’t know that I’d call it sad, exactly. I’ve been frustrated and worn out by the confusion, but not especially down in the way you mean, I don’t think.
Have you been feeling hopeless about your situation?
I’m not sure I’d say hopeless. I get upset because it’s hard to keep things straight, but I haven’t really thought of it as hopeless.
Have you been feeling anxious lately?
Not really anxious, no. I mean, I get bothered when I can’t remember something, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling anxious in general.
Have you noticed any difficulty with concentration or making decisions lately?

Yes, that’s really the main thing. My head just feels foggy, and I keep mixing up simple things—like appointment times, exhibit dates, or whether I already called a certain volunteer. It’s been hard to keep things straight.
Have you been having trouble remembering things that happened recently?

Yes, that’s part of it. I’ll forget things that just happened, or I’ll mix them up—like what time an appointment was, or the date for an exhibit, or whether I already called a volunteer. It’s like my head gets foggy and I can’t keep the recent things straight.
Do you have trouble recalling things that happened a few days ago?

Yes, I think so. A few days later things get jumbled—like I’ll mix up when an appointment was, or the date for an exhibit, or whether I already called a certain volunteer. My head just feels foggy and I can’t keep those simple things straight.
How long have you been experiencing this foggy feeling in your head?
It’s been about four months now, I think. It started around when the water damage happened and we got pushed into doing the remodel. Since then, my head’s just felt foggy.
Did you hit your head or injure your brain in any way around the time the water damage happened and you started feeling foggy?
No, I don’t think so. I don’t remember falling or hitting my head around then. It was more the house situation and everything getting disrupted, as far as I know.
Are you having trouble learning new information?

Yes, I think so. It’s like new things don’t stick the way they should. I’ll be told an appointment time or a date for an exhibit, or who I’m supposed to call, and then later I’ve got it mixed up or I can’t remember if I already did it. My head just feels foggy.
Have you experienced any significant medical issues or illnesses over the past year?
Not that I can think of. I haven’t had any major illness that I remember over the past year.
Did something unusual or traumatic happen to you around the time the water damage occurred and you started feeling foggy?
Not really, no. I mean, the water damage itself was upsetting and threw everything off, but I don’t remember anything unusual or traumatic happening to me around then.
Are you taking any medications currently?
I’m not sure I can list them off clearly right now. I’d have to check my bottles or my medication list to be accurate.
Did you experience any extremely stressful or disturbing events around the time the water damage happened?
I don’t think so. The water damage was stressful and frustrating, but I can’t recall anything extremely disturbing happening around that time.
Have you experienced any changes in your physical health around the same time your head started feeling foggy?

Yes… I have noticed I’m not eating much. Most days I just pick at some toast or maybe soup because food doesn’t really sound good. And my skirts have gotten looser, even though I haven’t been trying to lose weight.
Have you experienced any problems with your balance or coordination since your head started feeling foggy?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed myself falling or bumping into things more than usual. I just feel foggy, but my balance seems about the same.
How much weight would you say you've lost since you started feeling foggy and not eating as much?
I’m not exactly sure how many pounds. I haven’t been weighing myself. I just know I’m eating a lot less—mostly toast or soup—and my skirts are getting loose without me trying to lose weight.
Would you say you've lost more than 5% of your body weight since your head started feeling foggy?
I don’t know if it’s more than 5%. I haven’t checked my weight. I just know I’m eating very little—mostly toast or soup—and my skirts are looser without me trying to lose weight.
Are you having trouble performing your daily tasks or responsibilities due to this foggy feeling?

Yes, I am. I’ve missed some doctor visits, and I’ve gotten the senior center schedule all mixed up. My husband’s had to step in and help with phone calls and the calendar, and even decisions about repairs—things I used to handle myself.
Would you say your weight loss has been unintentional?
Yes, it has been. I’m not trying to lose weight. I just don’t feel like eating much most days—usually I only pick at some toast or soup—and my skirts have gotten loose.
